## 1. Recommendation

Build Effects v2 so a maker can recreate this kind of single-target, grid skill with **a few Simple controls and an Advanced timeline**, no code.

Do this, in order:

1. **Raise the step cap from 6 to 12**, and let Preview and exported games **play all 12**. Allow steps to **overlap** (a rune can stay on the ground while the rings shatter). The old BTF booth export still keeps only the first 6, with a notice. **ACCEPTED (Q3).**
2. **Keep the current preview layout** (the small top preview and the scrolling body). Add **scrubbing**, Play/Pause, and ½× / 1× under that preview. Do not make the preview the main canvas. **ACCEPTED (Q1: no).**
3. **Close the five suspected gaps**, and add flash tools plus photosensitivity handling: a stage-dim layer; additive glow blending; particles that can be pulled toward a point; a big ground-circle and orbit-ring asset; a Flash & shockwave kind with **no hard cap** (makers may build a strobe); a player setting **Reduce flashes**, forced on with reduced motion; and a `flash_risk` check that warns the maker and, for hub library games, shows a seizure warning before the game loads. **ACCEPTED (Q2, Q4, Q6).**
4. **Ship five new built-in pictures** (rune circle, orbit rings, spark, ember, smoke), generated by us, tagged **CC0**, safe to ship.
5. **Ship an “Astrologer awakening” preset** built from our own pictures and motion, with a credit to the clip, that uses **one soft flash** (our authoring choice, not a renderer cap). **ACCEPTED (Q5).**
6. **Export the effect as a standalone 2D asset**, and offer an **Asset only** door on the Home globe (name TBD; “Make assets” is suggested) that opens the designer with no game project. The animated preview defaults to **GIF**; WebP and APNG sit in Advanced. Packs have a **96-frame soft cap** with a warning. Game maker first; no 3D. See §8. **ACCEPTED (Q7, Q8, Q9).**

Leave for later, unless the CEO asks for them in this round: screen shake and zoom (the clip has neither, and we should not add them just to feel “bigger”); damage numbers (the clip has none; the existing `damage_label` stays off); a full multi-track editor beyond overlapping steps; ripping or tracing the reference sprites.

**Effort:** **L overall**, about **11–16 working days** of work across UX, the Keeper and the Engine Architect (was 8–12; standalone asset export adds about **3–4 days**). That work does **not** start on the effects player until hardening **H1–H4 is done**, unless the CEO reorders: there is **no effects renderer today**, only `src/fx/order`, and the CEO’s 13:38 order is H1→H4 first with the sprite track paused. Phase C (the new effects-player track) is therefore **queued after H4**. Format work (phase B) and designer chrome that does not need the real player can proceed. Risk is **medium-high**: the format change and the new player have to land together or the preset cannot play. Existing BTF looks must stay pixel-identical. Asset export depends on the same paint path, so it waits for phase C.

## 2. Beat-by-beat timeline (clip vs today)

Times are from the 8 fps stills (`frame-NNN` is at `(N-1) / 8` seconds). Named copies live at `ux/effects-v2-ref/beat-*.png`. The clip is one target on a grid. There is **no camera shake, no zoom and no damage numbers**. The caster (left) and the dummy (right) stay on their tiles. Wall torches and the floor dim; the two units and the effect stay lit.

| Beat | Time | What the stills show | Today (v1) | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0. Idle | 0.00–0.50 s | Lit grey floor, caster and dummy, no VFX. (`beat-0-idle-0.00s.png`) | Preview board can show two units. | None. |
| 1. Dim and charge | 0.50–1.00 s | Floor and walls go dark navy. Units stay at full brightness. Gold traces and an orbit path start to appear above the dummy. The caster holds a small gold ring. (`beat-1-dim-charge-0.75s.png`) | No stage-dim layer. Glow is a halo size in px, drawn normally, not as a room light. | **Stage dim** (terrain and props dim; units + this effect stay lit). |
| 2. Orb, rings and rune | 1.00–2.12 s | A large blue orb with three orbiting elliptical rings (gold, cyan, purple) floats above the dummy. A big multi-ring rune circle (gold outer, purple/cyan inner, chevrons) sits on the ground under the dummy, about **3–4 tiles wide**, in perspective. Strong additive glow. No ground layer (under units). | **Ground stamp** + **orbit-ring asset** + **additive blend** + a larger ground size. |

A few gold sparkles scatter. (`beat-4-point-light-3.38s.png`, `beat-4-drop-in-4.38s.png`, `beat-4-foot-rings-5.13s.png`) | `spawn: drop-on-tile` and `drop` height already exist, and a short shockwave could be faked with scale/fade if we had a ring picture. | Mostly covered once we have a drop step plus a small shockwave kind. (`beat-5-flash-invert-5.63s.png`, `beat-5-flash-white-5.88s.png`, `beat-5-shockwave-invert-6.00s.png`) | “Hit flash” is the impact burst colour, not a full-screen overlay. The engine also has a generic 2-frame **unit** hit flash (`unit-roster.clip_cues`), which is the wrong layer. No invert, no screen-wide shockwave. | **Flash & shockwave** as an overlay. The built-in preset uses **one soft flash**. Makers may author a strobe; the editor then flags `flash_risk` (see §6). |

**How many steps?** A faithful authoring of this clip is **9 overlapping steps** over about 8.4 s (see the preset in §7). Today the catalogue soft-caps `effect.steps` at 6, and **Preview and Render play only the first 6** (setup-format §2.10, project-format §6.7, the v1 designer copy). Steps are also **sequential**: there is no way for the rune to keep playing while a later shatter step runs. `layer_kind` is only a second motion *inside* one step. That is why “more than 6 steps in the preview” is a real gap, not just a nicer timeline.

## 3. Gaps, controls, format and engine

Keep the CEO’s order: **presets first → a few Simple controls → an Advanced step timeline**. Basic adds **zero extra taps** for ordinary looks. The two new Simple toggles appear only when the current effect actually uses them (the Astrologer preset does; Purple Drop does not). Effects still never change what an ability **does**.

### 3.1 Stage-dim layer

**User-facing.**  
- **Simple** (only if the effect has a dim step, or the preset turns it on): a toggle, **Dim the stage**, default on for Astrologer.  
- **Advanced:** step kind **Stage dim**, sliders **How dark** (0–85%, default 55%) and **Fade in / Fade out**. A one-line hint: “The floor and furniture go dark. Units and this effect stay lit.” No code.

**Keeper.** New step kind `dim`. Item fields: `dim_amount` stored as an **integer per-mille 0–850** (default 550; the slider still reads 0–85%), `dim_keep_units` (toggle, default true; v2 always keeps units and the playing effect lit — a per-prop glow opt-out comes later). Optional effect-level shortcut `stage_dim` (toggle) that the Simple control writes, `ui_derived` or a real knob that inserts/removes the dim step — preference: a real step, plus a Simple shortcut that toggles that step’s presence without exposing the timeline. Default off, so existing effects do not dim. Every new number field needs a range and a cap (see §11).

**Architect.** **Ruled, §13.1.** Terrain, props, map objects, weather, parallax and wall torches all dim. Units and the playing effect stay lit. Draw order: stage layers → dim → effect ground stamps → units → effect air → overlay (flash) → HUD.

**Performance.** One stage-rect fill or multiply. Negligible.

### 3.2 Additive glow blending

**User-facing.**  
- **Simple:** none. Colour and the existing glow size stay as they are.  
- **Advanced → Look**, or per step: **Blend: Normal / Add**. Presets that need it (Astrologer orb, sparks, flash) ship as Add. A short hint: “Add makes light pile up. Use it for orbs, sparks and flashes.”

**Keeper.** New item field `blend: "normal" | "add"`, default `"normal"`. Existing documents and BTF looks stay normal. Glow size (`glow`, `glow_size`, ramps) is unchanged.

**Architect.** **Ruled, §13.2.** `lighter` only for `blend: "add"`, drawn at **whole-pixel** positions with **nearest-neighbour** scaling. The **lite fallback is decided once when the effect starts and never changes mid-effect**.

**Performance.** Additive is cheap for a few sprites, expensive if applied to every smoke puff. Only glow, sparks, the orb, rings and the flash use it. Smoke stays normal.

### 3.3 Particles pulled toward a point

**User-facing.**  
- **Simple:** the existing **Count** shortcut can drive the first particle step’s count, as it already drives `orbit_count` / `row_count`.  
- **Advanced:** new step kind **Particles**, with **Motion: Burst out / Pull in / Spiral in / Rise**, **Count** (0–48, soft), **Life**, **Pull** (for pull-in and spiral-in; 0–2, how strongly they head at the anchor), **Picture** (spark, ember, smoke, or an upload). Anchor is already Caster or Target. Jitter and size spread reuse the existing spread fields.

**Keeper.** New kind `particles`. Fields: `particle_motion: "burst" | "attract" | "spiral-in" | "rise"`, `particle_count` (**0–48 soft** per effect, default 12, step 1; engine hard cap **96 overall** on a shared pool), `particle_life` in **ms** (with a stated min and max, e.g. 200–3000), `particle_pull` (0–2, default 1, with a cap). Reuse `anchor`, `jitter`, `start_spread`, `size_spread`, `picture`. The old `impact` / `sparks` / `impact_radius` burst stays for one-shot hit pops, so BTF looks do not move. We can later alias impact-sparks through this kind; not required for v2. Every new number field needs a range and a cap (see §11).

**Architect.** **Ruled, §13.3.** One **shared pool of 96**. Soft cap **48 per effect**, hard cap **96 overall**; the **oldest are dropped first**. Positions are **clock-based**, with a **seeded visual random stream**, so replays and previews match. Lite is chosen at start, never mid-effect (§3.8).

**Performance.** Astrologer uses ~24 spiral sparks, then ~8 smoke puffs + **12** embers, not at the same time as the peak spiral. **30 fps is plausible** with a low-res buffer, **but it is not promised**: it becomes an **acceptance test on a real mid-range phone**, with the lite fallback as the safety net.

### 3.4 More than 6 steps, and overlapping steps

**User-facing.**  
- **Simple:** no change. Speed still scales every step’s length.  
- **Advanced:** the timeline shows **all steps, including overlaps**, as blocks on a scrubbable bar (width = duration, left edge = start). **+ Add step** is never disabled up to 12. At 12: “12 steps is the most that plays, in Preview and in exported games.” Past 12 (if a hand-edited file has more): the extra steps are saved but dashed, same pattern as v1’s 7th step, and they do not play. Each step card gains **When it starts: After the last step / With the last step / At a time**, and a **Keep playing until the effect ends** toggle (hold). Sequential remains the default, so existing 2-step looks do not change.

**Keeper.** Raise `effect.steps` `max_items` from 6 to **12**, still soft. **Preview and Render play the first 12**, not 6. `toSkillSpec` / BTF booth export still slices to 6 with the existing notice. New item fields: `start_mode: "after-last" | "with-last" | "at-time"` (default `"after-last"`), `start_at` and `hold` in **ms**, rounded to ticks (the sliders may still read in seconds). For `after-last`, the Architect’s chain is `start = previous start + length + hold`. `hold` is a duration after the step’s length, not a rename of `connect`. A “Keep playing until the effect ends” control can be a UX shortcut that fills `hold`. Times have stated mins and maxes. No migration: missing fields = today’s sequential behaviour. Existing documents stay valid. **`connect` naming is open — see §11 Q8 and §13.6.**

**Architect.** **Ruled, §13.6**, except the **name** of chaining. Clock-based player on the engine’s **one clock** (never wall time). Overlap draw order: **layer, then start time, then document order**. The Architect used `connect` for “this step starts when the previous one ends”; that clashes with the existing hit-% knob. UX suggestion: keep `connect` as the hit %, and use `start_mode: "after-last"` for chaining.

**Performance.** 12 overlapping steps is fine if particle and additive caps hold. Do not start 12 particle systems at once; Astrologer doesn’t.

### 3.5 Big ground-circle and orbit-ring assets

**User-facing.**  
- **Simple:** the Astrologer preset sets the pictures. A single Picture row would be misleading (this look uses five pictures), so Simple shows **“Uses the built-in set”** and **Change** opens the picture picker only for the main air picture (the orb), or jumps to Advanced. Recommendation: Change edits the orb; rune / spark / ember / smoke stay Advanced.  
- **Advanced:** **Picture for this step** already exists (*proposed* in v1). New **Layer: Ground / Air / Overlay**. Ground draws under units (the rune). Air is today’s layer (orb, sparks). Overlay is full-screen (flash). New **Ground size** slider, 1–8 tiles, only on ground stamps (**ACCEPTED, Q6**). `scale` 0.35–2.6 stays for air pictures.

**Keeper.** Five new builtin picture ids (see §4), allowed on `effect.picture` and `steps[].picture`, licence `CC0-1.0`, shippable. New item fields: `draw_layer: "ground" | "air" | "overlay"` (default `"air"`), `ground_size` (1–8 tiles, default 3, step 0.25 or whole tiles if `scale_snap` is whole). New kind `stamp` (holds a picture on a layer with no flight path). Orbit rings can be a `stamp` on air with `spin` / a small `orbit_turns` rotation, or a generated 3-ellipse draw; prefer a picture plus spin so makers can swap it.

**Architect.** **Ruled, §13.4 and §13.7.** Draw order as in §13.1 (ground stamps after the dim, before units). Orbit rings are a **renderer helper**: the designer passes radii, thickness, tint and angle; the helper draws an integer midpoint ellipse and caches one bitmap per `(radii, thickness, tint, zoom)`. Rotation: **quarter turns in Basic**, **any whole degree in Advanced**.

**Performance.** Two large decals plus the 16 px particles. Cheap if the helper cache is used, not re-rasterised every frame.

### 3.6 Flash and shockwave (photosensitivity — detail in §6)

**User-facing.**  
- **Simple** (only if the effect has a flash step): toggle **Flash**, default on for Astrologer. If the player (or the editor preview) has **Reduce flashes** on, the toggle reads as on but the preview plays the reduced fallback, with the hint “Reduce flashes is on, so the white flash is skipped.”  
- **Advanced:** kind **Flash & shockwave**. Sliders: **Flash strength** (0–100%, **not clamped**), **Flash length** (a useful range, e.g. 0.04–2 s, **not capped at 0.12 s**), **Shockwave rings** (0–4, default 2), **Ring size**. Makers may add more than one flash step, including a strobe. No screen shake and no zoom are added for this kind (the Astrologer clip has neither); those stay out of v2 unless asked for later.  
- If the photosensitivity check trips, a **quiet notice** appears in the designer: the effect is marked `flash_risk`. It is **not a block**. The maker can keep the strobe.

**Keeper.** Kind `flash`. Fields: `flash_strength` (range and cap to set — today shown as 0–1, default 0.55), flash length in **ms** (recommend 40–2000, default 100 for the preset), `wave_rings` (0–4), `wave_radius` (0.5–8 tiles). **No keep-but-ignore clamp.** Values play as authored, unless the player has Reduce flashes on. See §6, §11 Q9 and the `flash_risk` flag.

**Architect.** **Ruled, §13.5.** No clamp; play as authored. `reduce_flashes` means **no white overlay, one shockwave ring, and a dip of at most 80 ms and 20%**. Reduced motion forces it on. The detector is one **shared pure engine function**, integer maths, run on the **effect document, not on pixels**. Output `{flashRisk, reasons:[tooMany|bigRed], worstWindowMs}`. The Keeper copies that flag to the effect, the project and the hub listing. Overlay draws after air, before the HUD. Do not reuse `unit-roster.clip_cues`.

### 3.7 Preview timeline and scrubbing

v1 deferred scrubbing (effect-designer §6). v2 still needs it: an 8-second, 9-step look cannot be judged with only Replay and ½×.

**ACCEPTED (Q1: no):** keep the **current preview layout** — the compact preview strip at the top, and the Simple / Advanced controls in the scrolling body below it. The preview does **not** become the main canvas, and the body does not become a 40% sheet for this screen.

Add, under that existing preview strip:

- A **playhead**: drag to scrub, tap a step block to jump there, Play/Pause, **½× / 1×** (keep Replay). Clock: `3.20 / 8.40 s`.  
- On Advanced, the same bar shows **overlapping blocks** (colour by kind: dim, ground, air, particles, flash). A red **hit** mark stays, now on the total length via `connect`.  
- Preview board for Astrologer: **5 × 4** (the 2 × 2 default is too tight for a 3–4 tile rune). Saved on the effect as today’s `booth_*` knobs.

The earlier 73e mocks that showed a large canvas and a 40% knob sheet were the rejected Q1 proposal. A later build should follow this section, not those shots, for layout. Scrubbing in those shots still stands.

### 3.8 Mid-range phone budget (summary)

| Budget | Value |
|---|---|
| Target device | Mid-range phone, 390×844, integer zoom 1–3 |
| Frame goal | 60 fps when possible. **30 fps is plausible** with a low-res buffer, **not promised**; it is an **acceptance test on a real mid-range phone** |
| Live particles | One shared pool of **96**. Soft cap **48 per effect**, hard cap **96 overall**; oldest dropped first. Clock-based positions, seeded visual random stream |
| Additive | `lighter` only for `blend: "add"`; whole-pixel positions, nearest-neighbour. Orb, rings, sparks, flash only |
| Lite fallback | **Chosen once when the effect starts, never changed mid-effect** (for example from `graphics` or a start-of-effect probe). Halve counts, 4 smoke puffs, additive only on the orb and the flash, skip spark trails |
| Reduced motion | Jump-cut stills at each beat (or a short cross-fade ≤ 80 ms), no auto-loop. **Reduce flashes is forced on** (§6, §13.5) |

## 4. New built-in assets

All five are **ours**, generated or drawn, **CC0**, safe to ship in exported games. They are not Kenney (unless a later pass finds a Kenney particle we prefer) and they are **not** traced from the clip. The library row reads **CC0 · TileEngine**. The v1 “Studio pack (pending)” / BTF pictures stay as they are and still may not ship.

| Id | Use | How it’s made | Source size | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rune-circle` | Ground stamp under the target | Drawn as pixel art, then a **generated** perspective ellipse (2:1) so it sits on the floor without a jagged rotate | **192 × 192** (square master), drawn at ~192 × 96 in perspective | 3 rings, chevrons, ticks. Tints with the effect colour. Covers ~3 tiles at 64 px; `ground_size` scales it to 1–8 tiles by integer zoom. |
| `orbit-rings` | Air, above the target | **Renderer helper** (§13.7): integer midpoint ellipses from radii, thickness, tint and angle; one cached bitmap per `(radii, thickness, tint, zoom)`. Not a rotated bitmap. | Logical **128 × 128** | Quarter turns in Basic, any whole degree in Advanced. |
| `spark` | Spiral-in shards; also reusable | Drawn pixel art, 2–3 frames | **16 × 16** sheet (16 × 48 if 3 frames) | Additive. One-pixel core, short streak. |
| `ember` | The ~12 lingering motes | Drawn pixel art, 2–3 frames | **8 × 8** (or 8 × 24 sheet) | Gold/cyan, additive, slower than sparks. |
| `smoke` | Post-flash wisps | Drawn pixel art, 3–4 frames, pre-dithered | **32 × 32** (or 32 × 128 sheet) | **Normal** blend, never additive. Soft, not a solid cloud. |

The generator (a small script, not a new studio) lives with the library build, so we can retint and regenerate without hand-editing PNGs. Uploads still follow `ux/art-upload.md` (see-through check, no stretch, ≤ 4096 px a side). Makers may replace any of the five with their own picture on a step.

## 6. Reduced motion, Reduce flashes, and `flash_risk`

**ACCEPTED (Q2, 14:42 card is final).** There is **no hard flash cap**. Makers **may** build strobe or seizure-risk flashes. The renderer does **not** clamp. The built-in Astrologer preset still uses **one soft flash** — that is our authoring choice, not a limit on other effects.

The reference clip’s hit (about three full-screen brightness swings plus colour inverts in ~0.6 s) is a photosensitivity risk. We do not copy that strobe into the preset, and we do not forbid a maker from building something like it.

**Reduce flashes** (player and editor setting — stays):

- Off by default.  
- **Forced on** when the player turns it on, **or** when `reduce_motion` is on, **or** when the device sends `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.  
- Fallback, when on: skip the white overlay entirely; keep **one** expanding shockwave ring and a short (≤ 80 ms) brightness dip of ≤ 20%.  
- The editor preview honours the same flag, and says so with a one-line hint. Exported games and hub play read the **player** setting, not an editor pref.

**Photosensitivity check (editor, not a block).** **Ruled, §13.5.** One shared pure engine function, integer maths, run on the **effect document, not on pixels**. It marks the effect `flashRisk` with `reasons: ["tooMany" | "bigRed"]` and `worstWindowMs`. The Keeper copies that to the effect, the project and the hub listing as `flash_risk`. A **quiet notice** is shown to the maker in the designer. Nothing is blocked, rewritten, or clamped.

- One **flash** = an overlay or `blend: "add"` step with a peak brightness change of **at least 10%** covering **at least 25%** of the reference screen (390×844 at the default zoom). One rise and fall is one flash; a hold adds nothing; loops count every time.  
- **tooMany:** more than 3 flash **starts** in any **1000 ms** window.  
- **bigRed:** `R×5 ≥ (R+G+B)×4` and covering at least 25%; **one is enough**.

**Hub library games.** If any effect in the game carries `flash_risk`, the hub shows a **seizure warning screen before the game loads**, with two buttons: **Continue** (play as authored) and **Reduce flashes** (turn the setting on, then load). The warning is not a block. Offline and non-hub play should still honour Reduce flashes when the player has it on; whether a local/sideloaded game also shows this screen is still a Keeper question.

**Where Reduce flashes lives.** `reduce_motion` is still **PROPOSED** in profile-format §3.7. Ask the Keeper to add **`reduce_flashes`** next to it (toggle, default false; forced on when reduced motion is on). Until that template is accepted, the editor may keep a device copy in `editor-prefs` for the designer preview only.

**Reduced motion, more generally.** Skip particle motion (show start and end stills, or a very short cross-fade). Holds can appear and disappear. Dim may ease over ≤ 80 ms or cut. The globe already forces a list when reduced motion is on; this follows the same idea: less motion, controls still visible.

## 7. “Astrologer awakening” preset

A new catalogue preset, **not** under the `btf-` family. Suggested id `te-astrologer-awakening`, display name **Astrologer awakening**, blurb: “The stage dims, a rune lights under the target, rings shatter into a point of light, then a single flash, smoke and embers.” Recipe: a new recipe `awakening` (or `cinematic-target`) so the 5 × 4 board and the five pictures travel with it.

**Credit line** (preset tile and describe text): “Inspired by @mozza_dev’s Astrologer awakening skill. Pictures and motion are TileEngine’s own.”

Proposed steps (9, overlaps, total ~8.4 s after a short idle). Times are authoring targets, not a frame-accurate copy.

| # | Name | Kind | Starts | Length | Hold / layer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Dim the stage | `dim` | 0.50 s (`at-time`) | 0.40 s fade-in | Hold until end; fade out from ~7.2 s | 55% dark, units lit |
| 2 | Rune circle | `stamp` | 0.70 s | 0.50 s fade-in | Hold; fade out by 5.40 s | Ground, `rune-circle`, size 3.5 tiles, normal + modest glow |
| 3 | Orb and rings | `stamp` | 0.80 s | 1.40 s | Air, additive | `orbit-rings` + generated orb, spin, scale up then hold |
| 4 | Rings shatter | `particles` | 2.10 s | 1.20 s | Air, additive, spiral-in | ~20 sparks, pull toward the point above the target |
| 5 | Point drops in | `straight` or drop | 3.25 s | 2.20 s | Air, additive | Small orb drops onto the target tile (`drop-on-tile`) |
| 6 | Foot rings | `flash` (rings only, strength 0) | 4.90 s | 0.60 s | Air | 2 small cyan rings, no white overlay |
| 7 | Flash and shockwave | `flash` | 5.50 s | 0.70 s (white ~0.10 s) | Overlay | **One** soft 55% flash + 2 large rings. No invert. Authoring choice, not a cap. This preset should **not** trip `flash_risk`. |
| 8 | Smoke | `particles` rise | 6.20 s | 2.00 s | Air, normal blend | 8 puffs, `smoke` |
| 9 | Embers | `particles` rise | 6.20 s (`with-last` or `at-time`) | 2.20 s | Air, additive | **12** `ember`s |

Simple controls for this preset: **Colour**, **Speed**, **Size** (the orb), **Dim the stage**, **Flash**. Hit reaction **None**, damage numbers **None**, no shake, no zoom. Count can nudge spark/ember counts, capped.

The mock freezes this look at the orb beat, the flash beat (one soft white, not the clip invert), and the Advanced 9-step timeline. **Credit and own-art preset ACCEPTED (Q5).**

## 8. Effects as standalone assets

**Addendum, 14:27 Europe/London.** TileEngine stays a **game maker first**. It should also be a tool people reach for when they only want **2D assets**: sprites that animate properly, a preview that updates as they work, and an export that works outside a game. No 3D. The converter and the generator keep their own tracks; this section is what Effects v2 adds to that reputation.

The designer still never changes what an ability does. An exported pack is pictures and timing, not rules.

### 8.1 Export with no game needed

The primary product is an **export pack**, written on the device, that another app can use with no TileEngine project and no engine runtime.

The pack always includes:

- A **PNG sprite sheet**, nearest-neighbour, **pixel-perfect integer scaling** only (×1, ×2, ×3, ×4). Non-integer sizes are refused, not blurred.
- A **JSON frame map** next to it: frame size, fps, and each frame’s `{x, y, w, h, duration}`. Credit and licence travel with it (`CC0` or `Yours`). The Keeper can pin the exact schema; it should stay small and documented, not a game document.
- A **transparent background** by default. The export is the **effect only** (rune, orb, sparks, smoke), not the floor and not the preview units. An Advanced toggle, off by default, can include the booth units as a guide.

The pack can also include, as ticks on the same screen:

- A **PNG sequence zip** (one file per frame, same map).
- An **animated preview**. **GIF is the default** (**ACCEPTED, Q8**). **WebP** and **APNG** are extras under Advanced. This is a preview for sharing and for checking the loop, not a substitute for the sheet + JSON.

The maker chooses **fps** (6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 24, 30) and **frame size** (32, 48, 64, 96, 128 px, square by default; a second side is Advanced). The preview and the sheet use the same numbers.

### 8.2 Asset only

An **Asset only** entry opens the Effect Designer **with no project**. Someone who just wants a sprite can pick a look, tweak it, and export, without first making a game. Work is kept in a **device-local asset library**, not in `effects/<id>.json` inside a project. “Save into a project” stays available if they later open or create one.

**ACCEPTED (Q7):** put Asset only on the **Home globe**, in the same list as the engine and the converter, so Basic users who want assets don’t have to start a project first. The on-globe **name is TBD**; **“Make assets”** is suggested. The designer chrome stays the same; the top bar reads “Asset only · No project”, and the main bottom action is **Export pack** rather than Save effect.

### 8.3 Loop-friendly mode

A **Loop** toggle sits on the export screen.

- Off (default for cinematic looks like Astrologer): the animation **plays once**.
- On: the preview and the animated file repeat.

A **seamless loop check** runs automatically when Loop is on, and can be run on demand when it is off. It compares the first and last frames (and a short wrap of two or three frames). The result is honest: “Seamless: first and last frames match” or “Not a seamless loop — first and last frames differ.” For Astrologer, this check **fails**, which is correct; it is a one-shot. The maker can keep Play once, or accept a visible pop, or add a short fade. We do not silently cross-fade and call it seamless.

### 8.4 Instant preview

A hard rule, in the designer and on the export screen: **every slider, toggle and swatch updates the visible preview within one frame. There is no Render button.** Ordinary changes never wait for a bake. Writing the pack to disk may take a moment on a long clip; that shows a short progress line, not a separate render step.

This is the same bar we want for the converter and the generator: you see the sprite move as you work.

### 8.5 Honest quality checks before export

Checks are warnings or blocks that say what will actually happen. Nothing is touched up in silence.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Scale is not an integer | **Block.** “This would blur. Use ×1, ×2, ×3 or ×4.” |
| Frame size is not a whole multiple of the source pixels | **Warn.** “Frames may go soft. Pick a size that keeps whole pixels.” |
| Animated GIF would need more than 256 colours, or heavy dither | **Warn.** “GIF will band these colours. WebP or APNG will stay closer to the preview.” |
| Frame count is over a **soft cap of 96** (**ACCEPTED, Q9**) | **Warn.** “101 frames is over the 96-frame soft cap. Export still works. Lower the fps or trim the length for a smaller pack.” (An 8.4 s effect at 12 fps is 101 frames, so Astrologer hits this at the default.) |
| Effect block would hold more than **64 frames** (hard cap, Architect H4 step 25, project-format r25 §6.7 K-4: the engine refuses `fxTooManyFrames`) | **Stopped in the editor, never at export.** Adding a frame or a step stops at 64 ("64 frames is the most an effect can hold"); an uploaded strip over 64 asks to keep the first 64. Not the same as the 96 soft cap above, which counts rendered export frames. |
| Loop is on, but the seamless check fails | **Warn.** “Not a seamless loop — first and last frames differ.” |
| The effect has a full-stage flash, and the background is transparent | **Warn.** “The flash is a white frame on a transparent sheet, and may look like a pop. Reduce flashes, or shorten the flash, if you don’t want that.” |
| Additive glow is flattened into a premultiplied PNG | **Note.** “Glow is baked into the pixels. It will not add on top of other art in another app.” |

Export stays enabled unless a check is a block (non-integer scale). The pack is still useful when a warning is open; the maker decides.

### 8.6 Phase and effort

This is **phase G**, after the effect can be drawn correctly (phases C–E), and therefore it also **waits for H4** unless the CEO reorders. It must reuse the same built bundle as the player (effect + time → draw list) for each transparent frame, so the sheet matches the in-engine look.

**Effort: M, about 3–4 working days** (UX about 2, including the Asset only door and the export screen; export raster and the JSON writer about 1–2, with the Architect). Added to the earlier 8–12, the v2 package becomes **about 11–16 days of work**, with the raster work **queued after H4 / phase C** unless the CEO reorders.

Risks particular to this phase: a 100-frame sheet on a mid-range phone (hence the soft cap and the honest warning); GIF banding on additive glows; confusing Asset only work with a project effect if the top bar is unclear.

## 9. Build phases, effort, risks

Work stays **offline-first**. Nothing ships until the CEO’s SEND on a finished round. The live designer is still the v1 mock in an iframe; a later build would replace that mock (and only then need `index.html` / shell wiring). This plan does not do that wiring.

**Queue, from the CEO’s 13:38 order.** The engine has **no effects renderer yet**. `src/fx/order` only reads and orders effect data. Phase C is a **new effects-player track**, not a small patch on an existing painter. Hardening **H1→H4 comes first**, and the sprite track is paused. **Effects-renderer steps (phase C, and anything that must call the real player: live Preview in D, asset-export raster in G) queue after H4**, unless the CEO reorders. Phase B (format) and designer chrome that can run against a stub may start earlier. The 11–16 working days are effort, not a start date.

Effects player** (new track) | Clock-based player on the engine’s one clock; pure function (effect + time → draw list) + thin painter; dim / additive (`lighter`, whole-pixel, nearest-neighbour) / shared 96 particle pool / flash (no clamp) / detector; lite chosen at start only. **Queued after H1–H4** unless the CEO reorders. Standalone asset export** | Home globe **Asset only** door (name TBD, “Make assets” suggested); export pack (PNG sheet + JSON, optional sequence zip; **GIF default**, WebP/APNG in Advanced); loop + seamless check; instant preview rule; honest preflight. Raster frames must use the same bundle as C, so this also **waits for H4 / phase C**. See §8. | **M**, ~3–4 days | C, D, E |

**Risks**

- **Photosensitivity**, if anyone authors a strobe (allowed). Mitigation: no clamp; detector marks `flash_risk`; quiet designer notice; hub pre-load seizure warning with Continue and Reduce flashes; honour `reduce_flashes` when it is on (§6).  
- **Copyright**, if we get too close to the reference art. Mitigation: own assets, credit the inspiration, never ship frames from the clip.  
- **The 6-step cap is load-bearing** for booth export and for “hit lands in the last step.” Mitigation: booth still slices to 6; **`connect` naming is open** (keep it as the hit %, preferably of total length; chaining is `start_mode: "after-last"`); no migration surprises.  
- **Overlap is a bigger mental model.** Mitigation: default stays sequential; Simple users only pick a preset; Advanced shows a clear Gantt bar.  
- **Performance** on mid-range phones if additive + 96 particles + a 4-tile decal meet zoom 6. Mitigation: shared 96 pool, 48 soft per effect, lite fallback **locked at effect start**, and a **30 fps acceptance test** on a real mid-range phone (not a promise).  
- **Existing looks must not move.** Every new field defaults to today’s behaviour.  
- **Iframe designer.** A build that only updates `mock-effects/` (or `mock-effects-v2/` wired in its place) is enough for a first playable; folding it into the shell is a later wiring task, not a format task.

## 13. Architect rulings

Recorded 2026-11-12, afternoon, Europe/London, in answer to §12. These are now the engine source of truth for Effects v2, alongside the CEO’s accepted scope.

**Track.** The engine has **no effects renderer yet**. `src/fx/order` only reads and orders effect data. This is a **new effects-player track**. The CEO’s 13:38 order is hardening **H1→H4 first**, with the sprite track paused, so the player and painter in this section **queue after H4** unless he reorders.

### 13.1 Dim

Yes. Terrain, props, map objects, weather, parallax and wall torches all dim. Units and the playing effect stay lit. A per-prop glow opt-out comes later, not in this track.

Draw order: **stage layers → dim → effect ground stamps → units → effect air → overlay (flash) → HUD**.

### 13.2 Additive

`lighter` for `blend: "add"` only, drawn at **whole-pixel** positions with **nearest-neighbour** scaling. The **lite fallback is decided once when an effect starts and never changes mid-effect**.

### 13.3 Particles

One **shared pool of 96**, with a soft cap of **48 per effect** and a hard cap of **96 overall**; the **oldest are dropped first**. Particles use their own **seeded visual random stream** and **clock-based positions**, so replays and previews match.

**30 fps is plausible** with a low-res buffer, **but it is not promised**. It becomes an **acceptance test on a real mid-range phone**, with the lite fallback as the safety net.

### 13.4 Layers

As in §13.1. Dim draws **before** units. Ground stamps draw **after** the dim and **before** units.

### 13.5 Flash and the detector

No clamp. `reduce_flashes` means **no white overlay**, **one shockwave ring**, and a dip of **at most 80 ms and 20%**. Reduced motion forces the setting on.

The detector is one **shared pure engine function** using **integer maths**, run on the **effect document, not on pixels**. The Keeper copies the flag to the effect, the project and the hub listing.

- One **flash** = an overlay or `blend: "add"` step with a peak brightness change of **at least 10%** covering **at least 25%** of the reference screen (390×844 at the default zoom). One rise and fall is one flash; a hold adds nothing; loops count every time.  
- **tooMany:** more than 3 flash **starts** in any **1000 ms** window.  
- **bigRed:** `R×5 ≥ (R+G+B)×4` and covering at least 25%; **one is enough**.  
- Output: `{flashRisk, reasons:[tooMany|bigRed], worstWindowMs}`.

### 13.6 Clock-based player, `connect` naming, overlap order

The player is **clock-based on the engine’s one clock** (never wall time). Start and hold are in **ms**, rounded to ticks.

The Architect redefines `connect` as “this step starts exactly when the previous one ends” (`start = previous start + length + hold`). **That clashes** with the existing catalogue meaning of `connect` (the % point where the hit lands) and with the earlier Keeper Q8. This is an **open naming decision**. See the shared question in §11 Q8 and at the end of §12.

UX suggestion: **keep `connect` as the hit %**, and treat that chaining as **`start_mode: "after-last"`**, which is already what “After the last step” means.

Overlap draw order: **layer, then start time, then document order**.

### 13.7 Orbit rings

A **renderer helper**. The designer passes radii, thickness, tint and angle; the helper draws an **integer midpoint ellipse** and caches one bitmap per `(radii, thickness, tint, zoom)`. Rotation: **quarter turns in Basic**, **any whole degree in Advanced**.

### 13.8 One player

**One player is required:** a **pure engine function** (effect + time gives a draw list) plus a **thin painter**. The designer’s Preview **must call the same built bundle**. There must not be a second mock player.

### §13.9 Connect naming — RESOLVED (Architect, 2026-11-12 14:49 London)
- `connect` stays the 0–1 hit point.
- Chaining is `start_mode: "after-last"`: start = previous start + length + hold. "Previous" = the step just before in document order. The sum is in whole ms, converted to ticks once at play time, rounding up (nothing starts early; no drift along a chain). A first step with after-last starts at 0.
- `with-last` and `at-time` are unchanged. The Architect's §12 wording that used `connect` for chaining is superseded. Keeper Q8 is now confirm-only.

## §16 Impact flash (CEO liked 15:19 London, via CoS) — PLAN ONLY
Source: @denchan_BSpro, [post](https://x.com/denchan_BSpro/status/2119914175925559724) (credit in the help text).
- **UI:** a one-tap toggle **"Impact flash"** on any effect (Basic, in the effect sheet, off by default). Advanced: circle size (1–8 tiles, default 3), centre (hit tile / caster / screen centre).
- **What it does:** inserts two frames at the hit (connect time, not effect start, so it lands on the impact; the CEO's "at the start" means the start of the impact): frame 1 is a white filled circle, frame 2 a black filled circle, then normal. One shot, never a strobe.
- **Data mapping (no new kind):** two `flash` steps with a circle shape at the hit, each flash_ms = 40 (min, ≈1 tick at 30 fps rounds up to 2 ticks / 67 ms), start_mode at-time = hit. Needs a `flash_shape: screen|circle` + `flash_radius` (tiles, 1–8) field (Keeper question K-IF1) and a black tint (existing step tint).
- **Reduce flashes on (player, or forced by reduced motion):** replaced by one soft fade: a single white circle at ≤30% alpha ramping to 0 over 150 ms; no black frame.
- **Flash detector:** white→black→normal over ≥25% of screen counts as up to 2 flashes. One impact flash is safe (limit is >3 per 1000 ms); two impact flashes within 1 s, or one plus the Astrologer flash, trips flashRisk. The designer shows the quiet notice; nothing is blocked (no maker cap).
- **Mock:** add a toggle row + 2-frame strip to mock-effects-v2 in the next mock round.
- **Open:** Keeper K-IF1 (flash_shape/flash_radius); Architect A-IF1 (circle fill in the shared player, integer radius, drawn in the overlay layer above units).
- **§16.1 (15:23)** The CEO 👍'd hit-moment timing (15:20). Architect A-IF1: yes. The circle is an integer midpoint fill drawn as horizontal spans, in the overlay layer. Detector correction: it counts flash STARTS, and a step counts only if it changes brightness by ≥10% and covers ≥25% of the 390×844 reference (radius ≳162 px). A smaller circle counts as 0. A big one counts as 2 (white + black; the return to normal isn't a start). Two big impacts within 1000 ms make 4, which trips flashRisk. White and black never trip big-red.


## §17 Feel tricks (CEO 🔥, 15:37 Europe/London, via CoS) — PLAN ONLY

Source research: `/workspace/share/effects-tricks/effect-tricks-research.md` (12 Nov 2026). Nothing here is built. Live `ui-shell` files are not touched. A build still needs the CEO’s SEND and **queues after H1–H4** unless he reorders.

§16 Impact flash stays as written. These seven sit next to it as a compact **Feel** row of one-tap toggles, plus two presets. Every toggle is **off by default**, so a maker who leaves them alone adds **zero extra taps** (the accepted Simple split in Q4 still holds: Dim and Flash are the only Simple kind-toggles; these Feel switches are optional extras, like Impact flash). Presets are picked the same way as Astrologer awakening.

**Screen shake and camera kick stay DEFERRED**, unless the CEO asks. The research ranks them as classic and cheap (Juice It or Lose It, Vlambeer’s Art of Screenshake, Stray Pixels), but this plan already left shake and zoom out because the Astrologer clip has neither. If they come back later: a Shake toggle with three strengths, directional, world-layer only, never the HUD, forced off by reduced motion. They are not a flash and are not a substitute for contrast, hit-stop or Impact flash.

Detector rules used below (Architect, §13.5 / §16.1): the detector counts flash **STARTS**, on the **effect document**, not on pixels. A step counts if it is an overlay or `blend: "add"` step with a peak brightness **change** of at least **10%** covering at least **25%** of the 390×844 reference at default zoom (a filled circle needs a radius ≳162 px). More than **3** starts in any **1000 ms** window sets `flashRisk` (`tooMany`). **bigRed** is `R×5 ≥ (R+G+B)×4` over at least 25%; one is enough. Loops count every time. A hold adds nothing. Output `{flashRisk, reasons:[tooMany|bigRed], worstWindowMs}`. Hub library games with `flash_risk` show the seizure warning before load (Continue, Reduce flashes).

Reduce flashes (player setting, or forced on by reduced motion): no white overlay, **one** shockwave ring, a dip of at most **80 ms and 20%**.

### §17.1 Explosion skeleton preset

**Source.** [Saint11, Explosions Part 1](https://saint11.art/img/pixel-tutorials/Explosion.gif), also listed at [saint11.art/blog/pixel-art-tutorials](https://saint11.art/blog/pixel-art-tutorials/) and [Explosions, part 1](https://www.patreon.com/posts/explosions-part-7719254). Colour and timing also match Slynyrd’s aerial explosion in [Pixelblog 31](https://www.slynyrd.com/blog/2020/12/14/pixelblog-31-shmup-sprite-design). A cheaper crescent-erode pop ([denchan, 28 Oct 2026](https://x.com/denchan_BSpro/status/2115565522079326511)) is an authoring tip for later, not a v2 field.

**Basic UI.** A built-in catalogue preset **“Explosion”** (suggested id `te-explosion`). One tap to pick it, like Astrologer. It is not applied to existing effects. Off by default in the sense that nothing gains these steps until the maker picks the preset.

**Advanced fields** (all with a range and a cap):

- Contrast / white disc size: **1–8 tiles**, default **3** (same `flash_radius` as §16).
- Blast size: **1–8 tiles**, default **4** (`ground_size` or stamp scale).
- Ember `particle_count`: **0–48** (soft; engine hard cap 96 overall), default **12**.
- Smoke `particle_count`: **0–48**, default **8**; `particle_life_ms` **400–3000**, default **1200**.
- Beat length for the two discs: `flash_ms` **40–200**, default **80** (Saint11’s GIF is 80 ms a frame), cap 200 for these two steps (the kind still allows up to 2000 elsewhere).
- Smoke `hold_ms` **0–20000**, default **400**; `fade_out_ms` **0–5000**, default **800** (after the hold, stamp only).
- Optional second blast: a delay `start_at_ms` **80–2000**, default **200** (0 / off unless the maker adds it). This is duplicated steps, not a new field.

**Mapping (no new kind).** A preset of overlapping existing steps, timed from the hit (`start_mode: "at-time"` at `connect` / `connect_step`, or the first step at 0 if the blast *is* the hit):

1. `flash`, dark tint, `flash_shape: "circle"`, overlay, `flash_ms` 80 — the contrast disc (“this will make other frames feel brighter”).
2. `flash`, white tint, same shape and radius, overlay, `start_mode: "after-last"` — the white punch. The §16 Impact flash toggle can still be stacked; the designer should quietly notice if the combined starts would trip `flashRisk`.
3. `stamp`, a sharp angular blast (proposed stock picture `blast-star`, CC0, same rules as the five planned pictures), `draw_layer` air, optional `blend: "add"` on a small core only, starts with the white disc or just after it.
4. `particles`, `particle_motion: "burst"`, stock `ember`, air, short life, with-last or a small `start_at_ms` offset.
5. `particles` (and/or a smoke `stamp`), `particle_motion: "rise"`, stock `smoke`, later start, longer life, `fade_out_ms` after the hold.

Fire leaves quickly; smoke leaves slowly. Do **not** loop this preset. A “second blast” in Advanced copies the stack with a short `start_at_ms` delay. `enabled` can hide a layer without moving later steps or the hit.

**Flashes?** **Yes, if the discs are large enough.** A 3-tile default circle is under the 25% / ≳162 px rule, so it counts as **0** starts (same as a small Impact flash). An 8-tile filled disc can count. Dark contrast is a brightness *change*, so a big dark disc is start 1 and a big white disc is start 2. Combined with a big Impact flash (2 more) inside 1000 ms that is 4 starts → `tooMany`. Default one-shot, 3-tile discs, should **not** trip. White / dark never trip `bigRed`; a saturated-red blast tint that covers ≥25% would. Default palette is white → yellow → orange, not big-red.

**Reduce flashes.** Skip the white overlay and the hard contrast disc. Keep **one** shockwave ring (see §17.2) plus the blast stamp, embers and linger smoke.

**Hub warning?** **Not on the default preset** (author it so `flashRisk` is false, like Astrologer). **Yes** if a maker enlarges the discs, stacks Impact flash, loops the preset, or tints a large additive blast big-red. Quiet notice, never a block.

---

### §17.2 Shockwave rings, using the ground-circle step

**Source.** [Slynyrd, Pixelblog 31](https://www.slynyrd.com/blog/2020/12/14/pixelblog-31-shmup-sprite-design). Inner / outer ring readability, and a lingering speed-lines layer, from [Stray Pixels, Breakpoint Explosion Breakdown](https://straypixels.net/breakpoint-explosion-breakdown/).

**Basic UI.** One toggle **“Shockwave”**, off by default, on the Feel row. When on, one **hollow** ring grows on the **ground** layer at the hit, using the **ground-circle** step (`stamp`, `draw_layer` ground). One tap.

**Advanced fields:**

- `radius_from`: **0–8 tiles**, default **0.5**.
- `radius_to`: **0.5–8 tiles**, default **4** (may share the cap with `ground_size` / `wave_radius`).
- `ring_thickness_px`: **1–16**, default **3**.
- Grow length: **150–800 ms** (r20: growth is max(150, len)), default **240**, cap **2000** (the stamp’s play length).
- `ease`: `"linear" | "fast-out"`, default **`"fast-out"`** (research: hot air races, then crawls as it cools — this default is deliberate; the toggle itself is still off).
- Second ring: off by default; if on, a second `stamp`, `draw_layer` air, thinner (`ring_thickness_px` 1–8, default 2), `radius_to` +1–3 tiles, delay `start_at_ms` **0–400**, default **80**.
- Tint: existing step tint (white-hot → warm → grey can be a later polish, not a v2 field). Optional `hold_ms` 0–20000 and `fade_out_ms` 0–5000 on the stamp.

Existing `wave_rings` (0–4) and `wave_radius` (0.5–8) on a `flash` step stay for an overlay ring; this toggle’s default path is the **ground stamp**, as requested. Reduce flashes already limits the *played* ring count to **one**, whichever path is used.

**Mapping.** One `stamp` at `start_mode: "at-time"` = the hit (`connect` / `connect_step`), `draw_layer` ground, picture a hollow ring drawn by the orbit / ellipse helper (integer midpoint ellipse, one cached bitmap per radii, thickness, tint, zoom — §13.7) or the planned ground-circle asset with a hole. The radius eases from `radius_from` to `radius_to` over the step length. Optional second stamp in air. Pairs with Impact flash, stage dim, and the Explosion preset. One-shot, not a pulse loop.

**Flashes?** **Usually no.** A thin hollow ring does not cover 25% of the reference screen. A large **filled** disc would. Keep it hollow and it should stay off the detector. Still one-shot.

**Reduce flashes.** Play **one** ring only (drop the second). No white overlay. The ground ring stays.

**Hub warning?** **Not at default** (hollow, one-shot). **Yes** only if a maker fills the disc, pulses or loops rings so more than 3 qualifying starts land in 1000 ms, or paints a large additive ring big-red.

---

### §17.3 Blank-frame punch

**Source.** [denchan, 29 Oct 2026](https://x.com/denchan_BSpro/status/2115927909806539043) (“ドット絵のエフェクトは「空白のフレーム」を入れると勢いが出る場合があります。例えばジェット噴射のエフェクトでは、空白を含めた計３フレームのみで表現することができます。”). Lightning waits: [Saint11, Electricity](https://saint11.art/img/pixel-tutorials/Electric.gif).

**Basic UI.** One toggle **“Blank punch”**, off by default. Inserts **one** empty frame at the hit. One tap. The timeline shows a hatched gap so the pause is visible.

**Advanced fields:**

- `blank_ms`: **40–200**, default **40** (the minimum tick-rounded window; about one frame), cap **200** so this cannot become a long blackout.
- `blank_at`: `"hit" | "step-start"`, default `"hit"`.

There is **no repeat field**. A lightning-style “wait, echo, wait” is authored as extra blank steps in Advanced. **Flag the flicker risk if it repeats:** a bright / blank / bright pattern is a flicker. If qualifying bright starts land more than 3 times in any 1000 ms window, that is `tooMany`. A lightning look should play **once**, never as an auto-loop.

**Mapping (no new kind).** A real step that draws nothing: a `stamp` with no picture (or an empty picture id), `enabled: true`, length `blank_ms`, `start_mode: "at-time"` at the hit (or at the start of the chosen stamp). It keeps its time slot, so `after-last` chaining is `start = previous start + length + hold` as already ruled. Prefer a real step over an effect-level flag, so the hatched gap is a first-class timeline block. Not `enabled: false` — that flag is for Simple kind-toggles that hide a step without being “a punch”.

**Flashes?** The blank **itself is not a flash start** (it is not an overlay or `blend: "add"` step). The bright step after it **is**, if that step changes brightness by ≥10% over ≥25% of the reference. **One** blank in a one-shot burst is fine. **Repeating** it can trip `tooMany`. The designer shows the quiet `flash_risk` notice when the document would fail; nothing is blocked.

**Reduce flashes.** **Never play the blank flicker.** Show a single static pose, or a soft fade / dip of at most 80 ms and 20% if there is also a flash. No bright / blank / bright.

**Hub warning?** **Not** for a one-shot blank. **Yes** if a repeating or looped blank-and-bright pattern trips `flashRisk`.

---

### §17.4 Hit-stop

**Source.** [Saint11, Impact](https://saint11.art/img/pixel-tutorials/Impact-export.gif) (pause **one frame** before a big impact, and no longer). [Sakurai, “Thinking About Hitstop”, Famitsu vols. 490–491, trans. Source Gaming](https://sourcegaming.info/2015/11/11/thoughts-on-hitstop-sakurais-famitsu-column-vol-490-1/) (both sides, same duration, scales with weight, **hard cap**). [Celeste Wiki, Freeze frames](https://celeste.ink/wiki/Freeze_frames) (at 60 fps: 3 / 6 / 9 frames = **50 / 100 / 150 ms**). Talk context: Vlambeer’s “Sleep” in [The Art of Screenshake](https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/vlambeer-co-founder-shares-advice-on-building-better-action-games) and [RPG Playground’s notes](https://rpgplayground.com/research-making-a-juicy-game/); a freezer slider up to 320 ms is noted in [gdad.wiki on Juice It or Lose It](https://gdad.wiki/wiki/sources/source-juice-it-or-lose-it) — we still cap at 150.

**Basic UI.** One toggle **“Hit-stop”**, off by default. When on, strength is **light, 50 ms**. One tap.

**Advanced fields:**

- `hit_stop_ms`: **0–150**, cap **150**, 0 = off. UI chips: **light 50**, **strong 100**, **finisher 150** (Celeste’s 3 / 6 / 9). No 320 ms slider. Applied at the hit (`connect` / `connect_step`).

**Mapping.** A timing flag on the hit step, not a drawn kind. The preview freezes the playing effect and the dummy unit for that window. In a game this **touches the engine’s one clock** (never wall time) — see A-T1. Start / hold / fade stay in ms, rounded up to ticks (50 ms may become 2 ticks / 67 ms at 30 fps; nothing starts early). Sakurai: attacker and victim freeze for the **same** duration. It often sits next to Impact flash or hit-white, but it is not itself a brightness change.

**Flashes?** **No.**

**Reduce flashes / reduced motion.** They are not the same switch: reduced motion forces Reduce flashes on, but hit-stop is a freeze, not a flash. **Reduced motion: skip the freeze entirely. Reduce flashes alone (motion still allowed): cap at 50 ms.**

**Hub warning?** **No.**

---

### §17.5 Smear frames

**Source.** [Wesnoth Wiki, How to create motion blurs](https://wiki.wesnoth.org/How_to_create_motion_blurs) (the smear is **100% opaque**, painted with the two brightest colours of the weapon, never a transparent blur). [Saint11, Motion Blur](https://saint11.art/img/pixel-tutorials/MotionBlur.gif) and [Attack Anim](https://saint11.art/img/pixel-tutorials/AttackSheet.gif). [Slynyrd, Pixelblog 9 – Melee Attacks](https://www.slynyrd.com/blog/2018/9/8/pixelblog-9-melee-attacks) and [Pixelblog 53 – Punches and Kicks](https://www.slynyrd.com/blog/2024/11/25/pixelblog-53-punches-and-kicks) (“usually a single smear frame can get the job done”).

**Basic UI.** One toggle **“Smear”**, off by default, on a stamp or travel step. One opaque smear frame at the hit, along the step’s path. One tap.

**Advanced fields:**

- `smear_ms`: **0–120**, default **40** when the toggle is on, 0 = off, cap **120** (few and fast).
- `smear_remnant`: bool, default **false**. If on, a thinner second frame, `smear_remnant_ms` **40–120**, default **40**.
- `smear_tiles`: **1–8**, default = the step’s travel capped at 8.

**Mapping (no new kind).** A stamp option plus a renderer helper: at the hit (`start_mode: "at-hit"`), draw an opaque fan / arc in the **air** layer that fills the actual 2D path (usually an ellipse, not a circle). The object snaps to the end of the arc in the same frame. Colours: the two brightest in the picture / tint, 100% opaque, no alpha blur. The orbit / ellipse helper can draw a thick pie slice, integer, cached. The remnant is a second, thinner `stamp`, `after-last`, optional `fade_out_ms` 0–5000. Reduced motion: skip the smear and show the end pose.

**Flashes?** **Usually no.** A huge white fan that covers ≥25% of the reference and lifts brightness by ≥10% would count as **one** start. Keep it on the weapon path.

**Reduce flashes.** Keep a short opaque smear if estimated coverage stays under 25%; otherwise the end pose only. Reduced motion always skips it (end pose).

**Hub warning?** **Unlikely** as a one-shot path smear. **Possible** if a maker loops or stacks a huge white / additive / big-red fan with other flash starts.

---

### §17.6 Hit-white

**Source.** [gdad.wiki summary of Juice It or Lose It](https://gdad.wiki/wiki/sources/source-juice-it-or-lose-it) (talk: [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Fy0aCDmgnxg); contemporary report: [Game Developer, 23 Aug 2013](https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/video-is-your-game-juicy-enough-)) — “the ball will get white every time it hits something.” [Saint11, Death / Take Hit](https://saint11.art/img/pixel-tutorials/Death.GIF) (a contrast frame; a *black* frame is also offered). Vlambeer’s “enemy flashes white” is listed in [RPG Playground’s notes on The Art of Screenshake](https://rpgplayground.com/research-making-a-juicy-game/). This is the character-side cousin of §16 Impact flash.

**Basic UI.** One toggle **“Hit-white”**, off by default. At the hit, the **target unit** is drawn as a flat white silhouette for one short window. One tap. Do not pulse it in Basic.

**Advanced fields:**

- `hit_white_ms`: **40–200**, default **40**, cap **200**.
- `hit_white_target`: `"target" | "caster" | "stamp"`, default `"target"`.
- `hit_white_mode`: `"white" | "tint" | "black"`, default `"white"`.

**Mapping (no new kind).** A unit (or stamp) **recolour on the units layer**, not an overlay `flash` step — so it does not sit above the whole stage, and the unit stays lit during a dim. Timed at `start_mode: "at-time"` = `connect` on `connect_step`. One shot, never a 10-hits-a-second pulse in the default controls.

**Flashes?** **Soft, usually no.** A single unit on a 1-tile body does not cover 25% of 390×844. A large boss or an 8-tile stamp can, and a white (or bright tint) recolour is a ≥10% brightness change, so that is **one** flash start. White and black never trip `bigRed`; a saturated-red mode over ≥25% would. One-shot is safe. A multi-hit combo that pulses this more than 3 times in 1000 ms is `tooMany`.

The detector runs on the **document**, not on pixels, so a unit recolour is invisible to it unless we teach it a coverage rule. Recommendation: count a start when the documented sprite size (tiles × default zoom on the 390×844 reference) covers ≥25% and the mode is a ≥10% brightness change. See A-T4 / K-T7.

**Reduce flashes.** No flat white (or black) body. A short coloured **outline**, or a dip of at most **20%** for at most **80 ms**.

**Hub warning?** **Not** for a one-shot on a normal unit. **Yes** if it is pulsed or looped into `tooMany`, or a huge saturated-red silhouette trips `bigRed`.

---

### §17.7 Shine with pickup sparkle

**Source.** Shine: [Saint11, Simple Shine](https://saint11.art/img/pixel-tutorials/Shine.gif) (rest about 500 ms, then a 4-frame diagonal band at 80 ms; an “extra shine” goes white → gold → leftover highlight → rest). Pickup: [Slynyrd, Pixelblog 24 – Items](https://www.slynyrd.com/blog/2019/12/21/pixelblog-24-items) (sparkle in place for currency and non-consumables; play on the character when the item changes the character; Hyper Echelon shares one **radial flash** language). Pickup types also appear in [Pixelblog 32](https://www.slynyrd.com/blog/2021/2/15/pixelblog-32-shmup-design-part-2).

**Basic UI.** Two one-tap entries, both off / unselected by default:

- Toggle **“Shine”** — plays a **simple** shine **once** on the current stamp or target (a white diagonal band, four 80 ms steps).
- Preset **“Pickup sparkle”** (suggested id `te-pickup-sparkle`) — simple shine + a few stock `spark` particles + one small radial ring. A **Heal** / **Level-up** tint variant can share this skeleton (green / cyan, play on the unit, no smoke).

**Advanced fields:**

- `shine_style`: `"simple" | "extra"`, default `"simple"`.
- `shine_ms`: **80–800**, default **320** (4 × 80), cap **800**.
- `shine_loop_rest_ms`: **0–5000**, default **0** (play once). A leisurely 500–2000 rest is the idle-item case. Looping **extra** shine is allowed but must go through the detector.
- `shine_angle`: **0–179°**, default **45** (diagonal), whole degrees (Advanced); Basic can leave it at 45.
- `shine_on`: `"stamp" | "target" | "caster"`, default `"stamp"` for the toggle, item tile for the Pickup preset, `"target"` for Heal / Level-up.
- Pickup sparks: `particle_count` **0–48**, default **6**; `particle_life_ms` **80–400**, default **200**; `particle_motion: "burst"` (a slight seed offset so a pile of coins does not lockstep).
- Radial ring: `radius_to` **0.5–3 tiles**, default **1** (keep it small), one-shot, hollow or a tiny `flash` circle that should stay under 25%.

**Mapping.** Shine is a renderer helper (a moving additive-or-normal diagonal band; no new picture required) drawn in **air** (or on the unit), clock-based, `start_mode` at-time or after-last. Extra shine adds a short white, then gold, then highlight on that same target — not a full-screen overlay. The Pickup preset is existing kinds: the shine helper, `particles` (stock `spark`, shared 96 pool, seeded stream), and a small ground or air ring (`stamp` / §17.2, or a tiny `flash` circle). Play once on collect; idle loop only with a long rest and **simple** style.

**Flashes?** **Simple shine: usually no** (a thin band). **Extra shine:** the full-white frame can be **one** start if the object covers ≥25%. A default 1-tile radial ring is **0**; a large additive radial flash can be 1. **Looping extra shine** on a big sprite counts **every** loop and can trip `tooMany`.

**Reduce flashes.** Keep the sparks and **one** small ring. No white overlay, no extra-shine full-white frame. A thin simple band may stay.

**Hub warning?** **Not** on the default preset or a one-shot simple shine. **Yes** if extra shine is looped on a large sprite, or a large radial flash (or a big-red tint) trips the detector.

Plan only. These are in addition to open K-IF1 (`flash_shape` / `flash_radius`) and the already-answered A-IF1 (circle fill). Every new number field needs a range and a cap in the setup-format table, in the units the player will use. Missing fields must equal today’s play (toggles off, no shine, no hit-stop), with no migration rewrite.

**Keeper**

**K-T1.** Please add a catalogue preset **Explosion** (suggested id `te-explosion`, not `btf-*`) as a skeleton of existing kinds only: a dark contrast `flash` circle, a white `flash` circle, a sharp blast `stamp`, ember `particles`, and later rising smoke (`particles` and/or a smoke `stamp` with `fade_out_ms`). Confirm a new stock picture id **`blast-star`**, licence `CC0-1.0`, shippable, allowed on `effect.picture` and `steps[].picture`, same rules as the five planned pictures. Default disc size 3 tiles, one-shot, no loop, and the shipped preset should not trip `flash_risk`. A “second blast” in Advanced is duplicated steps with a `start_at_ms` delay (80–2000, default 200), not a new field. `enabled` may hide a layer without moving later steps or the hit.

**K-T2.** The Explosion contrast and white discs, and any small radial pickup flash, need the same `flash_shape: "screen" | "circle"` and `flash_radius` (tiles, 1–8, default 3) already asked as **K-IF1**. Please confirm that one pair of fields covers §16 and §17, and that a dark tint on a `flash` step is just the existing step tint.

**K-T3.** For the **Shockwave** toggle, please add fields on a ground `stamp` (not a new kind): `radius_from` (0–8 tiles, default 0.5), `radius_to` (0.5–8, default 4), `ring_thickness_px` (1–16, default 3), and `ease: "linear" | "fast-out"` (default `"fast-out"`). The ring is hollow. A second ring is a second step. How do these relate to existing `wave_rings` (0–4) and `wave_radius` (0.5–8) on a `flash` step — keep both paths, or fold the overlay ring into the same radius fields?

**K-T4.** For **Blank punch**, please add `blank_ms` (40–200, default 40) and `blank_at: "hit" | "step-start"` (default `"hit"`). Recommended storage: a real step that draws nothing (a `stamp` with no picture, `enabled: true`, length `blank_ms`), so the timeline can show a hatched gap and `after-last` chaining stays `start = previous start + length + hold`. Please do not add a repeat field; makers who want lightning-style waits add more blank steps. How should an empty picture be written so it is valid and distinct from `enabled: false`?

**K-T5.** Please add `hit_stop_ms` (0–150, cap 150, 0 = off) on the **hit step** (`connect_step`), not as a second clock field on the effect. The UI exposes three strengths (50 / 100 / 150). Confirm range, cap, and that a missing field is 0.

**K-T6.** Please add smear fields, allowed on `stamp` (and, if you agree, on a travel motion step): `smear_ms` (0–120, 0 = off, default 0; the toggle writes 40), `smear_remnant` (bool, default false), `smear_remnant_ms` (40–120, default 40), `smear_tiles` (1–8, default the step’s travel capped at 8). The remnant may use `fade_out_ms` (already legal on stamp).

**K-T7.** Please add hit-white fields: `hit_white_ms` (40–200, default 40 when the toggle is on, 0 = off), `hit_white_target: "target" | "caster" | "stamp"` (default `"target"`), `hit_white_mode: "white" | "tint" | "black"` (default `"white"`). The detector is a pure function on the **document**, not on pixels. How should `flash_risk` see a unit recolour? I recommend counting a flash start when the documented sprite size (tiles at default zoom on the 390×844 reference) covers at least 25% and the mode is a ≥10% brightness change. Do you need an explicit coverage or tile-size field, or can the detector use existing size / `ground_size` / unit data already on the document?

**K-T8.** Please add shine fields: `shine_style: "simple" | "extra"` (default `"simple"`), `shine_ms` (80–800, default 320), `shine_loop_rest_ms` (0–5000, default 0 = play once), `shine_angle` (0–179, default 45), `shine_on: "stamp" | "target" | "caster"`. Please also add a **Pickup sparkle** preset (suggested id `te-pickup-sparkle`): simple shine, spark `particles` (default count 6, life 200 ms), and one small radial ring (radius 0.5–3, default 1). Heal / Level-up may be tint variants of the same skeleton (play on the unit, no smoke). Looping extra shine must remain visible to the computed `flash_risk` (loops count every time). The shipped presets should not trip `flash_risk`.

**Architect**

**A-T1. Hit-stop and the one clock.** The player is clock-based on the engine’s **one clock**, never wall time. A Feel toggle would freeze at the hit for `hit_stop_ms` (0–150, cap 150, rounded up to ticks). What does that pause — only this effect, the attacker and the victim (Sakurai: both sides, same duration), other playing effects, weather, or the HUD? Please do not add a second wall-time timer. If two effects request a stop in the same window, take the **max**, still capped at 150; do not stack. The designer Preview must use the **same built bundle** and freeze the dummy unit plus the effect. Reduced motion **skips** the freeze; Reduce flashes alone **caps it at 50 ms**. Is that workable on the one clock?

**A-T2.** For the Explosion preset and §16, please confirm the dark contrast disc and the white disc are both overlay circle fills (the integer midpoint span helper already ruled in A-IF1). A default 3-tile disc should be **0** flash starts; a disc that meets ≥10% brightness *change* and ≥25% coverage is one start each (dark + white = 2). The player must not loop this preset. Under Reduce flashes, skip both overlays and keep one ring plus blast, embers and smoke.

**A-T3.** Can the orbit / ellipse helper draw a **growing hollow ring** on the **ground** layer for Shockwave — integer midpoint ellipse, cached per (radii, thickness, tint, zoom), radius clock-eased from `radius_from` to `radius_to` with `ease: "fast-out"`? Reduce flashes plays one ring only. A hollow ring should normally be 0 flash starts; a filled large disc can count.

**A-T4.** A blank-punch step draws nothing for `blank_ms` (40–200, rounded up to ticks). Please confirm it is **not** itself a flash start. Repeating bright / blank patterns: each qualifying overlay or `blend: "add"` step is a start, and **loops count every time**, on the document. Under Reduce flashes, never play the blank flicker — a static pose or a soft ≤80 ms / 20% dip only.

**A-T5.** Please add a smear helper: one **100% opaque** fan / arc (never a transparent blur) along the step’s 2D path, in the two brightest colours of the picture / tint, integer, one frame (`smear_ms` 40–120), drawn in air; an optional thinner remnant frame after it. Reduced motion shows the end pose only. If a huge white fan could cover ≥25% of the 390×844 reference, should the document-side detector count it as a flash start, and how is coverage estimated without reading pixels?

**A-T6.** Hit-white is a **recolour on the units layer** (target, caster, or stamp) for `hit_white_ms`, not an overlay `flash`. Units stay lit during a dim. The detector runs on the document, not on pixels: please count a flash start when the documented sprite size at default zoom covers ≥25% of the 390×844 reference and the mode is a ≥10% brightness change. Under Reduce flashes: no flat white or black fill — a short outline, or a dip of at most 20% for at most 80 ms.

**A-T7.** Please add a shine helper (a moving diagonal band; extra style adds a short white → gold → highlight on that object, not a full-screen overlay) and play the Pickup preset through the **same** pure function (effect + time → draw list) plus thin painter, including spark particles on the shared 96 pool with the seeded visual stream. `shine_loop_rest_ms` is clock-based. The detector must see extra-shine full-white frames and large radial flashes, **including each loop**. Under Reduce flashes: sparks and one small ring; no white overlay and no extra-shine white; a thin simple band may stay. Lite fallback is still decided once when the effect starts.


## 17.10 Architect answers A-T1..A-T7 (2026-11-12, these queue after H4)

- **A-T1 Hit-stop:** never pauses the engine clock, command log or rules. It is a view-time offset, a pure function of (effect docs, clock time). Frozen things draw at the hit time while the window is open, then at clock time minus the frozen ticks. It freezes this effect, the attacker and the victim for the same length; other effects, weather, stage and HUD keep moving. If windows overlap, a unit unfreezes at the latest end, capped at 150 ms past the first freeze's start, and stops never stack. Reduced motion makes it 0, Reduce flashes alone caps it at 50 ms, and times are rounded up to ticks. The preview uses the same function on the dummy unit. Caveat for Modes: in a timed or RTS mode, a frozen unit's animation can lag its real state by up to 150 ms.
- **A-T2 Impact flash discs:** overlay circle fills. Coverage is πr² with r = tiles × tile px at default zoom, against 390×844. Each qualifying disc is 1 start, so dark plus white is 2. Looping is a document flag, and the Reduce flashes rule is as written.
- **A-T3 Shockwave rings:** the ellipse helper with a thickness, cached per (rx, ry, thickness, tint, zoom). Radius is a whole number each tick from an integer fast-out easing table. Coverage is outer area minus inner, so normally 0.
- **A-T4 Blank-frame punch:** a blank step is never a start. Bright steps count every time they play, loops included. An endless loop is expanded over a 1000 ms window plus one period.
- **A-T5 Smear:** an integer polygon fan fill, 100% opaque, one frame, in the air layer. Area = (sweep/360) × π × (outer² − inner²). Brightness is the fill's luma against a reference background of 128, or the dimmed luma when a dim step is on. A big white fan can be 1 start.
- **A-T6 Hit-white:** a recolour is 1 start per pulse when the sprite box at default zoom covers ≥25% and the luma change is ≥10% (white or black counts as full). Big-red uses the same box.
- **A-T7 Shine and pickup sparkle:** the band is clipped to the sprite box. Pickup goes through the same pure (effect, time) → draw-list function, with sparks from the shared 96 pool and the seeded visual stream. The detector counts shine white frames by sprite-box coverage and radial flashes as circles, every loop. Lite fallback is decided once at effect start.
- **General:** every Feel helper lives in fx and the renderer. None of it reaches core, the rules or the log.
- Still open: Keeper K-IF1 and K-T1..K-T8.

## 17.11 Keeper answers K-IF1, K-T1..K-T8 (setup-format r19 §2.10.2, b0a48154, PROPOSED)
These are outside the ACCEPTED §2.10.1. A build needs CEO SEND, and L47 goes after L46. The new start mode "at-hit" (start = hit + start_at_ms) replaces every "at-time = hit" in this plan.
- K-IF1: flash_shape screen|circle, flash_radius 1–8 tiles (default 3). The centre uses `anchor` (target, or the new value screen). The toggle writes white, then black at +40 ms, both at-hit.
- K-T1: te-explosion is 7 steps and has no flash_risk. blast-star is CC0 stock (CEO question F1). Air stamps scale 0.35–2.6. The 40–200 ms disc cap is a UI limit only.
- K-T2: one pair of fields covers §16 and §17; a dark disc is just the tint.
- K-T3: ring = flash_strength 0, wave_rings 1, draw_layer ground, wave_from (0–8, toggle 0.5), wave_thickness_px (1–16, default 3), look_ease "out", minimum 150 ms.
- K-T4: blank_ms 0 or 40–200 on a stamp with picture "none". blank_at is dropped and there's no repeat field.
- K-T5: hit_stop_ms 0–150 as an effect knob. It shifts view time only, and the detector uses 0.
- K-T6: smear_ms 0 or 40–120, smear_remnant_ms 0 or 40–120, smear_tiles 1–8 (null = auto).
- K-T7: hit_white_ms 0 or 40–200, hit_white_target target|caster|stamp, hit_white_mode white|tint|black. Coverage comes from the largest referencing unit's sprite box.
- K-T8: shine_ms 0 or 80–800 (toggle 320), shine_style, shine_loop_rest_ms 0–5000, shine_angle 0–179 (default 45), shine_on. te-pickup-sparkle is 3 steps with 0 flashes, and spark life minimum is 200 ms.

## 17.12 ACCEPTED: setup-format r20 (48b898b4), 2026-11-12 16:45 London
§2.10.2 Feel tricks is ACCEPTED. The CEO took F1–F3 as recommended at 16:43: blast-star is the sixth stock picture, the Impact flash disc stays at 3 tiles, and hit-stop is allowed in timed and real-time modes. This is plan only, with no build until Effects v2 gets SEND (after H1–H4).
- **at-hit start mode** (start = hit + start_at_ms) replaces every "at-time = hit" in this plan. If an at-hit step is at or before the hit step, it falls back to after-last with the atHitBeforeHit warning. Later after-last steps chain from at-hit steps as usual.
- **Hit-stop** is view time only. The effect, the attacker and the victim freeze for the same length; other effects, weather, the stage and the HUD keep moving. Overlapping freezes end at the latest end, capped at 150 ms past the first start. Reduced motion means 0, and Reduce flashes alone caps it at 50.
- **Blank** hides only this effect's other steps, never other effects, units or the HUD. It is never a flash start, and steps that resume after it count normally.
- **Shockwave growth** is max(150, len) ms, so the slider minimum is 150, not 80.
- **Flash detector** is te-flash@2, which gives the same result as @1 on old effects.
- **Fade (from §15.3/§15.4):** fade_out_ms runs AFTER the hold. §15.1 is struck through.

## §18 Roadmap after H2 (CEO order, 2026-11-12) — PLAN ONLY, no build now
- **Order:** first H3, trusted saves (step 24, written). Then H4, speed and memory (step 25). Then **the renderer, with the frame player and glow**. Sprite Studio frame-loop hardening runs in parallel with the renderer.
- **Rendering check-up** (part of the renderer step; the rules are already in ARCH §12.5):
  - whole-number zoom only;
  - a camera snapped to whole device pixels every frame;
  - `imageSmoothingEnabled = false`, set again after every resize, plus `image-rendering: pixelated`;
  - smooth fps on mid-range phones, measured on a real phone (60 when possible; 30 is the acceptance floor, as in the frame goal above).
- **Animated tiles and objects.** Every timer reads the one sim clock (no wall time).
  - **Water is a mix.** Painted frames by default (the code-drawn `water@2` style: 8 frames at 200 ms each). Optional colour cycling within the locked water ramp (the Atmosphere "shimmer"). An optional slow scroll for rivers.
  - **Trees and bushes sway** (a small looped sway, per object or per tile). They do not sway by default.
  - **Glow** (lights and the crystal's pulse) stays on its own soft layer above the crisp map.
  - Background in `/tmp/anim-tiles-audit.md`: today these exist only in the painter prototype, not in the engine.
- **Effect Designer "node mode"** (CEO-approved 2026-11-12 20:42). This is the future leap.
  - It comes **after the renderer and frame player** and is **optional**.
  - Nodes are small JS functions: noise, flow along a path, colour ramp, pixelate and motion trail.
  - Hand-drawn layers and sprites plug in as a node.
  - The graph is saved as plain data (nodes plus links), so it is safe to load and replay.
  - The normal layers-and-frames screen stays, as a preset graph underneath. Node mode evolves the current tool; it is not a new system.
  - Reference: Pixel Composer by @MakhamDev.
  - **No build now.**
